file_tia_scl.html:
Rules for SCL instructions

Instructions in SCL

SCL recognizes the following types of instructions:

  • Value assignments

    Value assignments are used to assign a tag a constant value, the result of an expression or the value of another tag.

  • Instructions for program control

    Instructions for program control are used to implement program branches, loops or jumps.

  • Additional instructions from the "Instructions" task card

    The "Instructions" task card offers a wide selection of standard instructions that you can use in your SCL program.

  • Block calls

    Block calls are used to call up subroutines that have been placed in other blocks and to further process their results.

Rules

You need to observe the following rules when entering SCL instructions:

  • Instructions can span several lines.

  • Each instruction ends with a semicolon (;).

  • No distinction is made between upper and lower case.

  • Comments serve only for documentation of the program. They do not affect the program execution.

Examples

The following examples shows the various types of instructions:

SCL

// Example of a value assignment

"MyTag":= 0;

// Example of a block call

"MyDB"();

// Example of a program control instruction

WHILE "Counter" < 10 DO

"MyTAG" := "MyTag" + 2;

END_WHILE;

See also

Basics of SCL

# T

| Rules for SCL instructions |

## Instructions in SCL

SCL recognizes the following types of instructions:

- Value assignments

  Value assignments are used to assign a tag a constant value, the result of an expression or the value of another tag.
- Instructions for program control

  Instructions for program control are used to implement program branches, loops or jumps.
- Additional instructions from the "Instructions" task card

  The "Instructions" task card offers a wide selection of standard instructions that you can use in your SCL program.
- Block calls

  Block calls are used to call up subroutines that have been placed in other blocks and to further process their results.

## Rules

You need to observe the following rules when entering SCL instructions:

- Instructions can span several lines.
- Each instruction ends with a semicolon (;).
- No distinction is made between upper and lower case.
- Comments serve only for documentation of the program. They do not affect the program execution.

## Examples

The following examples shows the various types of instructions:

```
// Example of a value assignment
"MyTag":= 0;
// Example of a block call
"MyDB"();
// Example of a program control instruction
WHILE "Counter" < 10 DO
    "MyTAG" := "MyTag" + 2;
END_WHILE;
```

**See also**

[Basics of SCL](https://docs.tia.siemens.cloud/r/MKsgSZvSoJDfAK_G3NxYhQ/W2NZ89cHm0pp51Veyuo42Q)

file_iox_admonition.html:
The presentation of your ST program data on the PLC's OPC UA Server is controlled by annotating your ST program with the appropriate pragmas. The OPC UA plugin for the ST Compiler (@ax/st-opcua.stc-plugin) validates the OPC UA configuration pragmas and generates a corresponding NodeSet XML document during a successful compilation.

Options that affect the server configuration as a whole are configured with pragma annotations above the configuration declaration.

Options that affect individual variable-mapping nodes are configured with pragma annotations above an individual variable or section of variables:

{OpcUa.NodeGenerator.IdType = SymbolName} // Use fully-qualified variable names as OPC UA NodeIds
CONFIGURATION PLC_1
  VAR_GLOBAL
    {S7.extern = ReadWrite} // Make var1 Read/Write accessible to the Web API and OPC UA Node Generator
    {OpcUa.AccessLevel = WriteOnly}  // Create an OPC UA node mapped to var1 with AccessLevel WriteOnly
    var1:INT;
  END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION

To install the OPC UA server configuration, the user must build an annotated ST program and load the program onto their PLC.

The configuration installed using ST Code Annotation will be named Server Interface_1.

Note

After building your AX project, the generated NodeSet XML file can be found in the project output directory under opcua/generated.xml.

# T

The presentation of your ST program data on the PLC's OPC UA Server is controlled by annotating your ST program with the appropriate pragmas. The OPC UA plugin for the ST Compiler (@ax/st-opcua.stc-plugin) validates the [OPC UA configuration pragmas](https://docs.industrial-operations-x.siemens.cloud/r/F2~cndjrEaWHpXLkY33djA/wbkXLoGiqUvjbTT_xPM91w) and generates a corresponding NodeSet XML document during a successful compilation.

Options that affect the server configuration as a whole are configured with pragma annotations above the [configuration declaration](https://docs.industrial-operations-x.siemens.cloud/access?ax:packageName=%40ax%2Fst-docs&ft:topicTitle=Configuration+declaration).

Options that affect individual variable-mapping nodes are configured with pragma annotations above an individual variable or section of variables:

```
{OpcUa.NodeGenerator.IdType = SymbolName} // Use fully-qualified variable names as OPC UA NodeIds
CONFIGURATION PLC_1
  VAR_GLOBAL
    {S7.extern = ReadWrite} // Make var1 Read/Write accessible to the Web API and OPC UA Node Generator
    {OpcUa.AccessLevel = WriteOnly}  // Create an OPC UA node mapped to var1 with AccessLevel WriteOnly
    var1:INT;
  END_VAR
END_CONFIGURATION
```

To install the OPC UA server configuration, the user must [build](https://docs.industrial-operations-x.siemens.cloud/access?ax:packageName=%40ax%2Fapax&ft:topicTitle=Apax+command-line+reference) an annotated ST program and [load](https://docs.industrial-operations-x.siemens.cloud/access?ax:packageName=%40ax%2Fsld&ft:topicTitle=load) the program onto their PLC.

The configuration installed using ST Code Annotation will be named `Server Interface_1`.

> **Note:** After building your AX project, the generated NodeSet XML file can be found in the project output directory under `opcua/generated.xml`.

# T

Use the [ICompilable service](https://docs.tia.siemens.cloud/r/tia1/topic-a) to compile a technology object.

## Requirement

The TIA Portal Openness application is connected to the TIA Portal. See [Siemens Industry Online Support](https://support.industry.siemens.com/cs/us/en/view/109760816).

## Program code: Compiling a technology object

```
ICompilable compileService = technologicalObject.GetService<ICompilable>();
CompilerResult result = compileService.Compile();
Console.WriteLine(result.State);
```

## Program code: Compiling the technology object group

```
TechnologicalInstanceDBGroup group = plcSoftware.TechnologicalObjectGroup;
  CompilerResult result = group.GetService<ICompilable>().Compile();
```

[![](https://docs.tia.siemens.cloud/api/khub/maps/tia1/resources/res-1/content?v=1)](https://docs.tia.siemens.cloud/viewer/attachment/tia1/res-1)

## Compile results

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| Success | No errors or warnings. |
| Error | Compilation failed. |

For the result object, see [CompilerResult](https://docs.tia.siemens.cloud/r/tia1/topic-b?section=).
